title.zh: 卷82 李琰之 祖瑩 常景
title.en: Volume 82: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, Chang Jing
title.raw: 卷82 李琰之 祖瑩 常景 Volume 82: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, Chang Jing

sentences.zh: 李琰之 祖瑩 常景

translations.literal: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, Chang Jing
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhi, Zu Ying, and Chang Jing

sentences.zh: 李琰之，字景珍，小字默蠡，隴西狄道人，司空韶之族弟。

translations.literal: Li Yanzhi, styled Jingzhen, childhood name Molü, a man of Dida in Longxi, a clansman of the Minister of Works Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhi, whose style was Jingzhen and whose childhood name was Molü, came from Dida in Longxi and was a kinsman of Minister of Works Li Shao.

sentences.zh: 早有盛名，時人號曰神童。

translations.literal: Early on he had great fame; people of the time called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: He won renown while still young, and his contemporaries hailed him as a child prodigy.

sentences.zh: 從父司空沖雅所歎異，每曰：「興吾宗者，其此兒乎？」

translations.literal: His father's cousin, Minister of Works Chongya, marveled at him and often said, "Will it be this boy who revives our clan?"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Li Chongya, who held the post of Minister of Works, was struck by his gifts and would often say, "Surely it is this boy who will raise our house again?"

sentences.zh: 恒資給所須，愛同己子。

translations.literal: He constantly supplied whatever was needed and loved him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: He always provided whatever Yanzhi required and cherished him as if he were his own son.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was recommended as a xiucai but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was nominated as a xiucai but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 曾遊河內北山，便欲有隱遁意。

translations.literal: He once traveled to the northern mountains within Henei and at once wished to withdraw into seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to the northern hills of Henei he conceived a desire to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 會彭城王勰辟為行臺參軍，[2]苦相敦引。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Pengcheng Xie summoned him as a staff officer on the mobile commandery, [2] and earnestly pressed him to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, then recruited him as an aide on his field headquarters staff [2] and urged him insistently to take the post.

sentences.zh: 尋為侍中李彪啟兼著作郎，修撰國史。

translations.literal: Before long, Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Biao recommended him as an associate historiographer to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Biao had him appointed as an associate historiographer charged with compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子博士，領尚書儀曹郎中，轉中書侍郎、司農少卿、黃門郎，修國史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University, concurrently served as a director in the Protocol Section of the Secretariat, then became Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture, and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, continuing to edit the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to become an Erudite of the Imperial University and head of the Protocol Section in the Secretariat, then served successively as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Minister of Agriculture, and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, all the while working on the national history.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，轉祕書監、兼七兵尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial University, then became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chancellor of the Imperial University, then Director of the Palace Library with the additional title of Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，太尉元天穆北討葛榮，以琰之兼御史中尉，為北道軍司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, Grand Marshal Yuan Tianmu marched north against Ge Rong; Yanzhi was made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and served as army supervisor on the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaozhuang, when Grand Marshal Yuan Tianmu campaigned north against Ge Rong, Yanzhi was given the concurrent post of Censor-in-Chief and appointed army supervisor for the northern column.

sentences.zh: 還，除征東將軍，仍兼太常。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, still concurrently serving as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After he came back he was named General Who Pacifies the East while retaining his concurrent duties as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 出為衞將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to office as General of the Guard and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as General of the Guard and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 頃之，兼尚書左僕射、三荊二郢大行臺。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was made concurrent Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Mobile Commandery over the three Jing regions and the two Ying regions.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and head of the grand mobile headquarters for the three Jing and two Ying circuits.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 琰之雖以儒素自業，而每語人言，吾家世將種，自云猶有關西風氣。

translations.literal: Although Yanzhi made his career as a plain scholar, he would tell people, "My family for generations has been a house of generals," and said of himself that he still had the spirit of the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yanzhi built his reputation as a scholar of plain dress and manners, he often told others, "Our house has bred generals for generations," and claimed that he still carried something of the old Guanxi warrior temper.

sentences.zh: 及至州後，大好射獵，以示威武。

translations.literal: Once he reached the province he took great delight in archery and hunting to display martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: After he took up his post in the province he threw himself into archery and the chase to display his martial bearing.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，南陽太守趙脩延以琰之莊帝外戚，誣琰之規奔蕭衍，襲州城，遂被囚執，脩延仍自行州事。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, the Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Xiuyan, because Yanzhi was a maternal relative of Emperor Xiaozhuang, slandered him as plotting to flee to Xiao Yan, attacked the provincial capital, and had him imprisoned; Xiuyan then administered the province on his own.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Zhao seized Luoyang, Zhao Xiuyan, prefect of Nanyang, denounced Yanzhi—who was related to Emperor Xiaozhuang by marriage—as planning to defect to Liang emperor Xiao Yan, stormed the provincial seat, and threw him in chains while he himself assumed control of the province.

sentences.zh: 城內人斬脩延，還推琰之釐州任。

translations.literal: The people within the city beheaded Xiuyan and in turn urged Yanzhi to put the province in order.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople killed Xiuyan and pressed Yanzhi to resume charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，徵兼侍中、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Deposed Emperor he was summoned as concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of the Palace, and Holder of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu first took the throne, Yanzhi was recalled to court as Attendant-in-Ordinary with the additional titles of General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of the Palace, and Holder of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Yongxi era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongxi (534).

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、雍州刺史，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of the Directorate of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the titles of Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, and Duke of the Secretariat, together with the governorship of Yong Province; his temple name was Wénjiǎn (Cultured and Unassuming).

sentences.zh: 琰之少機警，善談，經史百家無所不覽，朝廷疑事多所訪質。

translations.literal: Yanzhi from youth was quick-witted and skilled in discourse; he read without exception the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, and the court often sought his judgment on doubtful matters.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yanzhi was sharp and articulate; he had read his way through the classics, histories, and every major school of thought, and the court frequently turned to him when a doubtful point arose.

sentences.zh: 每云：「崔博而不精，劉精而不博，我既精且博，學兼二子。」

translations.literal: He often said, "Cui is broad but not refined; Liu is refined but not broad. I am both refined and broad, combining the learning of the two men."
translations.idiomatic: He liked to say, "Cui Guang is wide-ranging but lacks depth; Liu Fang is deep but lacks breadth. I am deep and broad alike—I unite the strengths of both."

sentences.zh: 謂崔光、劉芳也。

translations.literal: He meant Cui Guang and Liu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He was speaking of Cui Guang and Liu Fang.

sentences.zh: 論者許其博，未許其精。

translations.literal: Critics granted his breadth but not his refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators conceded his breadth but not his depth.

sentences.zh: 當時物議，咸共宗之。

translations.literal: Public opinion of the time all regarded him with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion united in treating him as a master.

sentences.zh: 又自誇文章，從姨兄常景笑而不許。

translations.literal: He also boasted of his literary compositions, but his cousin on his mother's side Chang Jing laughed and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He was equally fond of praising his own writing, though his maternal cousin Chang Jing would only smile and withhold his assent.

sentences.zh: 每休閑之際，恒閉門讀書，不交人事。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure he always shut his door to read books and had no dealings with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his free hours he invariably shut himself in to read and kept clear of worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「吾所以好讀書，不求身後之名，但異見異聞，心之所願，是以孜孜搜討，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: He once told someone, "The reason I love to read is not to seek a name after death, but because strange sights and strange reports are what the heart desires; therefore I search and investigate tirelessly and cannot make myself stop.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to a friend, "I read not for posthumous fame but because every new sight and story is something my heart craves; that is why I hunt through books without rest and cannot bring myself to stop.

sentences.zh: 豈為聲名勞七尺也？

translations.literal: How could it be to wear out a seven-foot frame for reputation's sake?
translations.idiomatic: Surely I am not wearing out my body merely for the sake of renown?

sentences.zh: 此乃天性，非為力強。」

translations.literal: This is inborn nature, not forced effort."
translations.idiomatic: It is my nature, not something I force upon myself."

sentences.zh: 前後再居史職，無所編緝。

translations.literal: Though he twice held historiographical office, he compiled nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though he twice held a post in the historiography office, he left nothing compiled.

sentences.zh: 安豐王延明，博聞多識，每有疑滯，恒就琰之辨析，自以為不及也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anfeng Yanming was broadly informed and greatly learned; whenever he had doubts he always went to Yanzhi for analysis and considered himself inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yanming of Anfeng, himself widely read, would bring every knotty question to Yanzhi for clarification and freely admitted that he could not match him.

sentences.zh: 二子綱、惠，並從出帝入關。

translations.literal: His two sons Gang and Hui both followed the Deposed Emperor in entering the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Gang and Hui both followed Emperor Xiaowu west into the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 祖瑩，字元珍，范陽遒人也。

translations.literal: Zu Ying, styled Yuanzhen, was a man of You in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ying, whose style was Yuanzhen, came from You in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敏，仕慕容垂為平原太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Min served Murong Chui as Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Min had served Murong Chui as prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中山，賜爵安固子，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified Zhongshan, he was granted the title Viscount of Angu and appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, Min was ennobled as Viscount of Angu and appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously awarded Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously named governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，字元達。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ni, styled Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zu Ni, styled Yuanda.

sentences.zh: 以從征平原功，進爵為侯，位馮翊太守，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit in the campaign at Pingyuan he was advanced to Marquis, held the post of Administrator of Fengyi, and was posthumously awarded Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the Pingyuan campaign he was raised to marquis, served as prefect of Fengyi, and after death was granted the governorship of You Province.

sentences.zh: 父季真，多識前言往行，位中書侍郎，卒於安遠將軍、鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: His father Jizhen was well versed in words and deeds of former ages; he held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and died while serving as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jizhen knew the lore of earlier ages inside out; he had been Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and died in office as General Who Pacifies the Distance and prefect of Julu.

sentences.zh: 瑩年八歲，能誦詩書，十二，為中書學生。

translations.literal: At eight years Ying could recite the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents; at twelve he became a student of the Palace Secretariat school.
translations.idiomatic: At eight Ying could recite the Odes and Documents from memory; at twelve he entered the Palace Secretariat school.

sentences.zh: 好學耽書，以晝繼夜，父母恐其成疾，禁之不能止，常密於灰中藏火，驅逐僮僕，父母寢睡之後，燃火讀書，以衣被蔽塞窗戶，恐漏光明，為家人所覺。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was addicted to books, continuing day into night; his parents feared he would fall ill and forbade him but could not stop him. He would secretly hide fire in the ashes, drive off the servants, and after his parents had fallen asleep light a fire to read, blocking the windows with clothing and bedding lest light leak out and the household discover him.
translations.idiomatic: He was so devoted to study that he read on through the night; when his parents, fearing illness, forbade it he could not obey. He would hide embers in the ash-pit, send the servants away, and once his parents slept would kindle a lamp, muffling the windows with quilts so no gleam betrayed him to the household.

sentences.zh: 由是聲譽甚盛，內外親屬呼為「聖小兒」。

translations.literal: Because of this his reputation was very great, and relatives within and without the family called him the "holy child."
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread accordingly, and kinsmen near and far nicknamed him the "little sage."

sentences.zh: 尤好屬文，中書監高允每歎曰：「此子才器，非諸生所及，終當遠至。」

translations.literal: He especially loved composing literature; Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Yun often sighed and said, "This boy's talent and capacity are beyond what the students can match; in the end he will go far."
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of writing, and Gao Yun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, would often exclaim, "This child's gifts outstrip every other student—he is bound to go far."

sentences.zh: 時中書博士張天龍講尚書，選為都講。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Secretariat Erudite Zhang Tianlong lectured on the Documents; Ying was chosen as head lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tianlong of the Palace Secretariat lectured on the Documents, Ying was chosen to serve as head discussant.

sentences.zh: 生徒悉集，瑩夜讀書勞倦，不覺天曉。

translations.literal: When the students had all assembled, Ying, weary from reading through the night, did not notice that dawn had come.
translations.idiomatic: The students had all gathered, but Ying, exhausted from a night of reading, failed to notice daybreak.

sentences.zh: 催講既切，遂誤持同房生趙郡李孝怡曲禮卷上座。

translations.literal: The urging to lecture was pressing, so he mistakenly took up on the lectern his fellow student's Li Xiaoyi of Zhao commandery's volume of the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed to begin the lecture, he by mistake carried to the dais his roommate Li Xiaoyi's copy of the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 博士嚴毅，不敢還取，乃置禮於前，誦尚書三篇，不遺一字。

translations.literal: The erudite was stern and strict; he dared not go back to fetch the correct book, so he set the Rites before him and recited three chapters of the Documents without omitting a single character.
translations.idiomatic: The erudite was a stern man, and Ying dared not step down to fetch the right text; he laid the Rites on the desk and from memory recited three chapters of the Documents without missing a word.

sentences.zh: 講罷，孝怡異之，向博士說，舉學盡驚。

translations.literal: When the lecture ended, Xiaoyi marveled at it and told the erudite; the whole school was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: After the session Xiaoyi told the erudite what had happened, and the entire academy was astounded.

sentences.zh: 後高祖聞之，召入，令誦五經章句，並陳大義，帝嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu heard of it, summoned him in, ordered him to recite passages from the Five Classics and set forth their larger meaning; the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen heard the story he summoned Ying to court, had him recite passages from the Five Classics and explain their larger meaning, and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 瑩出後，高祖戲盧昶曰：「昔流共工於幽州北裔之地，那得忽有此子？」

translations.literal: After Ying had left, Emperor Gaozu jested with Lu Chang, saying, "In old times Gong Gong was banished to the northern borderlands of You Province—how could such a boy suddenly appear there?"
translations.idiomatic: After Ying withdrew, the emperor teased Lu Chang: "Did we not exile Gong Gong to the far north of You—whence this prodigy?"

sentences.zh: 昶對曰：「當是才為世生。」

translations.literal: Chang replied, "Surely talent is born for the age."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang answered, "Surely genius appears when the times require it."

sentences.zh: 以才名拜太學博士。

translations.literal: On account of his talent and fame he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of his reputation he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 徵署司徒、彭城王勰法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed acting aide in the Legal Section under the Minister of Works, the Prince of Pengcheng Xie.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as acting aide in the legal bureau of the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, who held the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖顧謂勰曰：「蕭賾以王元長為子良法曹，今為汝用祖瑩，豈非倫匹也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu turned to Xie and said, "Xiao Ze took Wang Yuanzhang as legal aide for Ziliang; now I have given you Zu Ying—is this not a match in kind?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Xie and said, "Xiao Ze gave his son Ziliang Wang Yuanzhang as legal aide; I have given you Zu Ying—is that not a fair match?"

sentences.zh: 敕令掌勰書記。

translations.literal: He ordered him to take charge of Xie's correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Ying to manage the prince's correspondence.

sentences.zh: 瑩與陳郡袁翻齊名秀出，時人為之語曰：「京師楚楚，袁與祖；

translations.literal: Ying and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery were equally famed and outstanding; people of the time made a saying: "In the capital, splendid—Yuan and Zu;
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery stood equal in fame; contemporaries coined a rhyme: "In the capital, splendid pair—Yuan and Zu;

sentences.zh: 洛中翩翩，祖與袁。」

translations.literal: In Luoyang, graceful—Zu and Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: in Luoyang, graceful pair—Zu and Yuan."

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Secretariat Aide in the Three Excellencies Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to a secretariat post in the Three Excellencies section.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王肅曾於省中詠悲平城詩，云：「悲平城，驅馬入雲中。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Su once in the office recited a poem Lament for Pingcheng, saying, "Lament for Pingcheng—driving horses into Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, Director of the Secretariat, once recited in the office his "Lament for Pingcheng": "Lament for Pingcheng—we drive our horses into Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 陰山常晦雪，荒松無罷風。」

translations.literal: On the Yin Mountains snow is always dim; on the wild pines the wind never ceases."
translations.idiomatic: On the Yin Mountains snow never lifts; on the barren pines the wind never rests."

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰甚嗟其美，欲使肅更詠，乃失語云：「王公吟詠情性，聲律殊佳，可更為誦悲彭城詩。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Xie greatly admired its beauty and wished to have Su recite again, but in a slip of the tongue said, "Your Lordship's lyrical temperament and tonal rules are exceptionally fine—could you recite again the Lament for Pengcheng poem?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng admired the verses and asked Wang Su to recite again, but in his enthusiasm he misspoke: "Your Lordship's feeling for verse and mastery of tone are superb—please recite once more your 'Lament for Pengcheng.'"

sentences.zh: [3]肅因戲勰云：「何意悲平城為悲彭城也？」

translations.literal: [3] Su thereupon jested with Xie, saying, "Why turn Lament for Pingcheng into Lament for Pengcheng?"
translations.idiomatic: [3] Wang Su teased the prince: "Since when is 'Lament for Pingcheng' the same as 'Lament for Pengcheng'?"

sentences.zh: 勰有慚色。

translations.literal: Xie showed embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: The prince flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 瑩在座，即云：「所有悲彭城，王公自未見耳。」

translations.literal: Ying was present and at once said, "There is indeed a Lament for Pengcheng—Your Lordship simply has not seen it."
translations.idiomatic: Ying, who was present, spoke up at once: "A 'Lament for Pengcheng' does exist—Your Lordship has simply never heard it."

sentences.zh: 肅云：「可為誦之。」

translations.literal: Su said, "You may recite it for us."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said, "Then let us hear it."

sentences.zh: 瑩應聲云：「悲彭城，楚歌四面起；

translations.literal: Ying answered on the spot, "Lament for Pengcheng—Chu songs rise on every side;
translations.idiomatic: Ying answered without hesitation: "Lament for Pengcheng—Chu songs rise on every side;

sentences.zh: 屍積石梁亭，血流睢水裏。」

translations.literal: Corpses pile up at Shiliang Pavilion; blood flows in the Sui River."
translations.idiomatic: corpses heap at Shiliang Pavilion; the Sui River runs red with blood."

sentences.zh: 肅甚嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Su greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su marveled and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 勰亦大悅，退謂瑩曰：「即定是神口。

translations.literal: Xie was also greatly pleased; on retiring he said to Ying, "You are truly a divine mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted as well; afterward he told Ying, "You truly have a god's tongue.

sentences.zh: 今日若不得卿，幾為吳子所屈。」

translations.literal: Had I not had you today, I would nearly have been put down by Master Wu."
translations.idiomatic: If you had not been here today, I would almost have been bested by that fellow from Wu."

sentences.zh: 為冀州鎮東府長史，以貨賄事發，除名。

translations.literal: He served as chief clerk of the Eastern Garrison of Ji Province but was struck from the rolls when a bribery affair came to light.
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk of the Eastern Garrison in Ji Province he was stripped of office when a bribery scandal broke.

sentences.zh: 後侍中崔光舉為國子博士，仍領尚書左戶部。

translations.literal: Later Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang recommended him as Erudite of the Imperial University, and he still headed the Left Household Section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cui Guang, Attendant-in-Ordinary, had him appointed Erudite of the Imperial University while he continued to head the Left Household Section of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李崇為都督北討，引瑩為長吏。

translations.literal: When Li Chong was Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign he took Ying as his chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong commanded the northern campaign he took Ying on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 坐截沒軍資，除名。

translations.literal: He was punished for seizing army supplies and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again for embezzling military stores.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he became Vice Director of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed Vice Director of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，於廣平王第掘得古玉印，敕召瑩與黃門侍郎李琰之令辨何世之物。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era an ancient jade seal was unearthed at the residence of the Prince of Guangping; an edict summoned Ying and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Li Yanzhi to identify from what age the object came.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era an ancient jade seal was dug up at the mansion of the Prince of Guangping; the court ordered Ying and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Li Yanzhi to determine its date.

sentences.zh: 瑩云：「此是于闐國王晉太康中所獻。」

translations.literal: Ying said, "This was presented by the King of Khotan in the Taikang era of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "This was a gift from the king of Khotan, presented in the third year of Jin Taikang (282)."

sentences.zh: 乃以墨塗字觀之，果如瑩言，時人稱為博物。

translations.literal: They then rubbed ink over the characters to read them, and it was indeed as Ying had said; people of the time called him broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Ink was rubbed over the inscription to bring out the characters, and the result matched Ying's account exactly; contemporaries hailed him as a walking museum.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子祭酒，領給事黃門侍郎，幽州大中正，監起居事，又監議事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Chancellor of the Imperial University, concurrently Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Service Section, Grand Rectifier of You Province, overseer of the imperial diary, and also overseer of deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Chancellor of the Imperial University, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Service Section, Grand Rectifier of You Province, overseer of the imperial diary, and overseer of court deliberations.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以瑩為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Ying was made Director of the Palace Secretariat in the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao seized Luoyang, Ying was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat in the Hall.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，坐為顥作詔，罪狀尒朱榮，免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Ying was punished for drafting an edict for Hao indicting Erzhu Rong and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhuang regained the palace, Ying was dismissed for having drafted Yuan Hao's indictment of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 後除祕書監，中正如故。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Director of the Palace Library, his rectifier post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed Director of the Palace Library while retaining his post as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 以參議律曆，賜爵容城縣子。

translations.literal: For participating in deliberations on the calendar he was granted the title Viscount of Rongcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on the calendar reforms he was ennobled as Viscount of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 坐事繫於廷尉。

translations.literal: For an offense he was detained by the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was later imprisoned on a criminal charge.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝遷車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Under the Former Deposed Emperor he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，莊帝末，尒朱兆入洛，軍人焚燒樂署，鍾石管弦，略無存者。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, soldiers burned the Music Office; bells, stones, and string and wind instruments were nearly all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, when Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, his troops burned the Music Office and destroyed nearly every bell, stone chime, and orchestral instrument.

sentences.zh: 敕瑩與錄尚書事長孫稚、侍中元孚典造金石雅樂，三載乃就，事在樂志。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ying, together with Recorder of the Secretariat Affairs Changsun Zhi and Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Fu, to supervise the making of refined music with bells and stones; after three years it was completed—the matter is recorded in the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: The court charged Ying, together with Changsun Zhi, who recorded Secretariat affairs, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Fu, with rebuilding the court's bell-and-stone music; the work took three years and is recorded in the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及出帝登阼，瑩以太常行禮，封文安縣子。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Ying as Minister of Ceremonies performed the rites and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Ying as acting Minister of Ceremonies conducted the accession rites and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 天平初，將遷鄴，齊獻武王因召瑩議之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era, when the court was about to move the capital to Ye, the Prince of Qi, Xianwu, thereupon summoned Ying to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era, as the court prepared to move the capital to Ye, Prince Xianwu of Qi summoned Ying to consult on the plan.

sentences.zh: 以功遷儀同三司，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Holder of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was named Holder of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈尚書左僕射、司徒公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Duke of the Directorate of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the titles of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Duke of the Secretariat, and governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 瑩以文學見重，常語人云：「文章須自出機杼，成一家風骨，何能共人同生活也。」

translations.literal: Ying was esteemed for literary learning and often told people, "Writing must come from one's own loom and shuttle and achieve a family style and bone—how can one live together with others?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying was renowned for his literary gifts and often said, "A writer must weave from his own loom and forge a distinctive voice—how can one simply live off another man's lines?"

sentences.zh: 蓋譏世人好偷竊他文，以為己用。

translations.literal: This was in mockery of people who love to steal others' writings and use them as their own.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to mock those who pilfer other people's compositions and pass them off as their own.

sentences.zh: 而瑩之筆札，亦無乏天才，但不能均調，玉石兼有，製裁之體，減於袁、常焉。

translations.literal: Yet in Ying's own compositions there was no lack of native genius, but he could not achieve even balance; jade and common stone were mingled, and the shaping of his style fell short of Yuan and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's own writings were not without genius, yet he could not sustain an even tone: jade and pebble lay side by side, and in finish and control he fell short of Yuan Fan and Chang Jing.

sentences.zh: 性爽俠，有節氣，士有窮厄，以命歸之，必見存拯，時亦以此多之。

translations.literal: By nature he was forthright and chivalrous, with moral fiber; when scholars in destitution entrusted their lives to him, he would surely preserve and rescue them, and people of the time also praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature open-handed and high-spirited; when scholars in distress placed their fate in his hands he always saved them, and contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 其文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子珽，字孝徵，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ting, styled Xiaozheng, inherited [the title].
translations.idiomatic: His son Ting, styled Xiaozheng, succeeded to his rank.

sentences.zh: 常景，字永昌，河內人也。

translations.literal: Chang Jing, styled Yongchang, was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing, whose style was Yongchang, came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 父文通，天水太守。

translations.literal: His father Wentong was Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wentong had been prefect of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 景少聰敏，初讀論語、毛詩，一受便覽。

translations.literal: Jing from youth was clever; when he first read the Analects and the Mao version of the Odes, after one reading he could survey them all.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Jing was quick-witted; the first time he read the Analects and the Mao Odes he could recite them from memory.

sentences.zh: 及長，有才思，雅好文章。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had literary talent and elegantly loved composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he matured he showed literary gifts and a deep love of writing.

sentences.zh: 廷尉公孫良舉為律博士，高祖親得其名，既而用之。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Gongsun Liang recommended him as Erudite of Law; Emperor Gaozu personally learned his name and soon afterward employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Gongsun Liang recommended him as Erudite of Law; Emperor Xiaowen heard his name and soon took him into service.

sentences.zh: 後為門下錄事、太常博士。

translations.literal: Later he served as Recorder in the Chancellery and Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a recorder in the Chancellery and as an Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 正始初，詔尚書、門下於金墉中書外省考論律令，敕景參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengshi era an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to examine and discuss statutes at the outer office of the Palace Secretariat at Jinyong; Jing was ordered to participate in the deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengshi era the court ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to review the legal code at the outer secretariat office at Jinyong, and Jing was directed to take part.

sentences.zh: 世宗季舅護軍將軍高顯卒，其兄右僕射肇私託景及尚書邢巒、并州刺史高聰、通直郎徐紇各作碑銘，並以呈御。

translations.literal: The younger uncle of Emperor Shizong, General Who Protects the Army Gao Xian, died; his elder brother Right Vice Director Zhao privately commissioned Jing, together with Director of the Secretariat Xing Luan, Governor of Bing Province Gao Cong, and Direct Attendant Xu He, each to compose an epitaph, and all were presented to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu's uncle by marriage, General Who Protects the Army Gao Xian, died, his elder brother Gao Zhao, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, privately asked Jing, Xing Luan of the Secretariat, Gao Cong the governor of Bing, and Xu He a direct attendant each to draft an epitaph; all four texts were submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗悉付侍中崔光簡之，光以景所造為最，乃奏曰：「常景名位乃處諸人之下，文出諸人之上。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong handed them all to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang to select; Guang judged Jing's composition the best and memorialized, "Chang Jing's rank and position stand below the others, but his writing rises above them all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave all four to Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang for judgment; Guang ranked Jing's piece highest and reported, "Chang Jing ranks below the others in office, yet his prose surpasses them all."

sentences.zh: 遂以景文刊石。

translations.literal: Jing's text was therefore cut into stone.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's text was carved on the stele.

sentences.zh: 肇尚平陽公主，未幾主薨，肇欲使公主家令居廬制服，付學官議正施行。

translations.literal: Zhao had married the Princess of Pingyang; before long the princess died, and Zhao wished to have the princess's household steward observe mourning in the mourning shed in full dress, entrusting the matter to the academic officials to deliberate and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had married the Princess of Pingyang; when she died soon afterward he wanted her household steward to observe the full mourning rites in the mourning shed and referred the question to the ritual scholars for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 尚書又以訪景，景以婦人無專國之理，家令不得有純臣之義，乃執議曰：「喪紀之本，實稱物以立情；

translations.literal: The Secretariat also consulted Jing; Jing held that a woman has no principle of exclusive rule over the state, and a household steward cannot have the status of a pure minister, and therefore argued, "The root of mourning regulations truly names things in order to establish feeling;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat also asked Jing's view; he held that no woman may hold sovereign authority and that a household steward cannot be a full minister in the ritual sense, and argued as follows: "The foundation of mourning law is to name things so as to express feeling;

sentences.zh: 輕重所因，亦緣情以制禮。

translations.literal: what lightness and heaviness depend on also follows feeling in regulating ritual.
translations.idiomatic: degrees of severity likewise follow feeling in shaping ritual.

sentences.zh: 雖理關盛衰，事經今古，而制作之本，降殺之宜，其實一焉。

translations.literal: Although principle touches rise and decline and affairs pass through past and present, the root of establishment and the fitness of increase and decrease are in substance one.
translations.idiomatic: Though principle spans rise and fall and practice changes with the ages, the root of ritual making and the rule of graded increase and decrease are in essence the same.

sentences.zh: 是故臣之為君，所以資敬而崇重；

translations.literal: Therefore a subject serving a lord is to supply reverence and exaltation;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a subject serves a lord, the rites supply reverence and heighten esteem;

sentences.zh: 為君母妻，所以從服而制義。

translations.literal: serving a lord's mother or wife is to follow mourning dress and regulate righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: serving a lord's mother or wife is to follow graded mourning and fix the proper measure of duty.

sentences.zh: 然而諸侯大夫之為君者，謂其有地土，有吏屬，無服文者，言其非世爵也。

translations.literal: Yet when feudal lords and grandees are called lords, it means they possess land and soil and have official subordinates; where there is no mourning text, it means they are not hereditary enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: When feudal lords and grandees are called 'lords,' it is because they hold land and retain officials; where no mourning text applies, it means they are not hereditary fiefs.

sentences.zh: 今王姬降適，雖加爵命，事非君邑，理異列土。

translations.literal: Now when an imperial princess descends in marriage, although titles are added, the affair is not a lord's fief, and the principle differs from enfeoffed territory.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial princess marries down, titles may be conferred, yet the case is not a lord's domain and differs in principle from a territorial fief.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 諸王開國，備立臣吏，生有趨奉之勤，死盡致喪之禮；

translations.literal: When princes open states they fully establish ministers and clerks; in life there is the toil of attendance, in death the full performance of mourning rites;
translations.idiomatic: Princes who receive states establish full ministerial staffs; in life their servants attend them, in death they perform the full mourning rites;

sentences.zh: 而公主家令，唯有一人，其丞已下，命之屬官，既無接事之儀，實闕為臣之禮。

translations.literal: but the princess's household steward is only one man, and his assistants and below are appointed subordinate officials; they have neither the ceremony of receiving affairs nor in truth the ritual of being ministers.
translations.idiomatic: but a princess's household steward is a single officer, and his assistants and subordinates are merely appointed staff; they lack the protocol of public service and truly lack the status of ministers.

sentences.zh: 原夫公主之貴所以立家令者，蓋以主之內事脫須關外，理無自達，必也因人。

translations.literal: Tracing why the princess's nobility establishes a household steward, it is because the mistress's inner affairs, when they must touch the outer world, by principle cannot reach it on their own and must rely on another person.
translations.idiomatic: The reason a princess appoints a household steward is that domestic affairs sometimes require contact with the outside world, which she cannot manage alone and must delegate to another.

sentences.zh: 然則家令唯通內外之職，及典主家之事耳，無關君臣之理，名義之分也。

translations.literal: Thus the household steward only handles duties connecting inner and outer and manages the mistress's household affairs; he has nothing to do with the principle of lord and minister or the division of names and roles.
translations.idiomatic: The steward's charge is only to mediate between inner and outer quarters and manage the household—nothing to do with the lord-minister relation or the formal division of roles.

sentences.zh: 由是推之，家令不得為純臣，公主不可為正君明矣。

translations.literal: From this it follows that the household steward cannot be a pure minister, and that a princess cannot be a true lord is clear.
translations.idiomatic: It follows that the steward cannot be a full minister and that a princess cannot be a true sovereign—this is plain.

sentences.zh: 且女人之為君，男子之為臣，古禮所不載，先朝所未議。

translations.literal: Moreover, a woman as lord and a man as minister is not recorded in ancient ritual, nor debated by former courts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a woman as sovereign and a man as her minister appears nowhere in ancient ritual and was never debated by earlier courts.

sentences.zh: 而四門博士裴道廣、孫榮乂等以公主為之君，以家令為之臣，制服以斬，乖謬彌甚。

translations.literal: Yet Erudites of the Four Gates Pei Daoguang, Sun Rongyi, and others took the princess as their lord and the household steward as their minister, prescribing the severest hemp mourning—an error all the more extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Erudites Pei Daoguang and Sun Rongyi of the Four Gates treated the princess as sovereign and the steward as minister, prescribing the severest hemp mourning—an error all the graver.

sentences.zh: 又張虛景、吾難羈等，不推君臣之分，不尋致服之情，[4]猶同其議，準母制齊，求之名實，理未為允。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Xujing, Wu Nanji, and others did not deduce the division of lord and minister or seek the feeling behind mourning dress; [4] they still agreed with that opinion, equating it with mourning for a mother at the highest grade—in name and substance the principle is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xujing, Wu Nanji, and others likewise failed to weigh the lord-minister distinction or the grounds for mourning dress; [4] they still sided with that view, equating the case with mourning for a mother at the highest grade—in name and fact the ruling cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 竊謂公主之爵，既非食菜之君；

translations.literal: I venture to say the princess's enfeoffment is not a lord who receives a fief;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that a princess's title is not a fief-holding lord;

sentences.zh: 家令之官，又無純臣之式。

translations.literal: the office of household steward likewise has no form of a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: nor does the office of household steward fit the model of a full minister.

sentences.zh: 若附如母，則情義罔施；

translations.literal: If attached as to a mother, then feeling and righteousness have nowhere to apply;
translations.idiomatic: If treated as mourning for a mother, feeling and duty have no proper object;

sentences.zh: 若準小君，則從服無據。

translations.literal: if measured as to a lesser lord's wife, then following mourning has no basis.
translations.idiomatic: if measured as mourning for a lord's principal wife, the graded mourning has no basis.

sentences.zh: 案如經禮，事無成文；

translations.literal: According to the canonical rituals, the matter has no established text;
translations.idiomatic: According to the canonical rites, no established text covers this case;

sentences.zh: 即之愚見，謂不應服。」

translations.literal: in my humble view, I say mourning should not be worn."
translations.idiomatic: in my humble view, mourning should not be worn."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his ruling.

sentences.zh: 景淹滯門下積歲，不至顯官，以蜀司馬相如、王褒、嚴君平、揚子雲等四賢，皆有高才而無重位，乃託意以讚之。

translations.literal: Jing lingered in the Chancellery for many years without reaching a prominent office; taking the four worthies of Shu—Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, Yan Junping, and Yang Ziyun—who all had lofty talent but no weighty position, he entrusted his meaning to eulogize them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing spent years in the Chancellery without reaching high office; thinking of the four Shu masters—Sima Xiangru, Wang Bao, Yan Junping, and Yang Xiong—each gifted yet never granted great rank, he wrote eulogies to express his sympathy.

sentences.zh: 其讚司馬相如曰：「長卿有艷才，直致不羣性。

translations.literal: His eulogy for Sima Xiangru says, "Changqing possessed brilliant talent and a nature upright and beyond the herd.
translations.idiomatic: His eulogy for Sima Xiangru runs: "Changqing bore radiant genius and a nature upright, apart from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 鬱若春煙舉，皎如秋月映。

translations.literal: Luxuriant as spring mist rising, bright as the autumn moon shining.
translations.idiomatic: Rich as spring mist rising, bright as autumn moonlight.

sentences.zh: 遊梁雖好仁，仕漢常稱病。

translations.literal: Though he wandered in Liang and loved benevolence, serving Han he often pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered in Liang and loved virtue, yet serving Han he often pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 清貞非我事，窮達委天命。」

translations.literal: Pure integrity was not his affair; poverty and success he entrusted to Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Integrity was not his concern; fortune and failure he left to fate."

sentences.zh: 其讚王子淵曰：「王子挺秀質，逸氣干青雲。

translations.literal: His eulogy for Wang Ziyuan says, "The prince bore an outstanding nature; his free spirit pierced the blue clouds.
translations.idiomatic: His eulogy for Wang Ziyuan runs: "The prince stood forth in splendid grace; his free spirit reached the azure clouds.

sentences.zh: 明珠既絕俗，白鵠信驚羣。

translations.literal: A bright pearl already beyond the vulgar, a white swan truly startling the flock.
translations.idiomatic: A bright pearl beyond the common world, a white swan that truly startled the flock.

sentences.zh: 才世苟不合，遇否途自分。

translations.literal: If talent and the age do not accord, meeting fortune or misfortune each finds its own path.
translations.idiomatic: When talent and the age fail to meet, fortune and misfortune each go their own way.

sentences.zh: 空枉碧鷄命，徒獻金馬文。」

translations.literal: In vain he wasted the mandate of the Green Cock; in vain he offered writings at the Golden Horse Gate."
translations.idiomatic: In vain he answered the Green Cock summons; in vain he offered his writings at the Golden Horse Gate."

sentences.zh: 其讚嚴君平曰：「嚴公體沉靜，立志明霜雪。

translations.literal: His eulogy for Yan Junping says, "Lord Yan's person was deep and still; his resolve was clear as frost and snow.
translations.idiomatic: His eulogy for Yan Junping runs: "Lord Yan was deep and still of bearing; his resolve shone clear as frost and snow.

sentences.zh: 味道綜微言，端蓍演妙說。

translations.literal: Tasting the Way he gathered subtle words; with divining stalks upright he unfolded wondrous discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He savored the Way and gathered subtle teachings; with yarrow in hand he unfolded profound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 才屈羅仲口，位結李強舌。

translations.literal: Talent bent before Luo Zhong's mouth; position tied Li Qiang's tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Talent bowed to Luo Zhong's eloquence; rank silenced Li Qiang's tongue.

sentences.zh: 素尚邁金貞，清標陵玉徹。」

translations.literal: In plain dress he surpassed golden integrity; his clear mark towered over jade brilliance."
translations.idiomatic: In plain dress he surpassed golden integrity; his pure renown outshone jade's gleam."

sentences.zh: 其讚揚子雲曰：「蜀江導清流，揚子挹餘休。

translations.literal: His eulogy for Yang Ziyun says, "The Shu River leads clear currents; Yangzi draws the remaining blessings.
translations.idiomatic: His eulogy for Yang Xiong runs: "The Shu River leads clear streams; Yangzi draws its lingering grace.

sentences.zh: 含光絕後彥，覃思邈前修。

translations.literal: Holding light he surpassed later talents; deep thought left earlier cultivators far behind.
translations.idiomatic: Holding his light, he outshone later talents; in deep thought he left earlier sages behind.

sentences.zh: 世輕久不賞，玄談物無求。

translations.literal: The age slighted him long without reward; in abstruse discourse he sought nothing from things.
translations.idiomatic: The age long slighted him without reward; in subtle discourse he sought nothing from the world.

sentences.zh: 當途謝權寵，置酒獨閑遊。」

translations.literal: On the road to power he declined favor and privilege, set out wine and wandered at leisure alone."
translations.idiomatic: He declined power and favor on the high road, poured wine, and wandered alone at leisure."

sentences.zh: 景在樞密十有餘年，為侍中崔光、盧昶、游肇、元暉尤所知賞。

translations.literal: Jing was in the inner secretariat for more than ten years and was especially known and rewarded by Attendants-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, Lu Chang, You Zhao, and Yuan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jing served in the inner secretariat for more than a decade and won particular favor from Attendants-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, Lu Chang, You Zhao, and Yuan Hui.

sentences.zh: 累遷積射將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to General of Accumulated Archery and Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to General of Accumulated Archery and Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，東宮建，兼太子屯騎校尉，錄事皆如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yan chang era the Eastern Palace was established; he was made concurrent Commandant of Cavalry for the Heir Apparent, his recorder duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yan chang era, when the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed concurrent Commandant of Cavalry for the Heir Apparent while retaining his recorder duties.

sentences.zh: 其年受敕撰門下詔書，凡四十卷。

translations.literal: That year he received an edict to compile Chancellery edicts, forty volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was ordered to compile Chancellery edicts, forty volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 尚書元萇出為安西將軍、雍州刺史，請景為司馬，以景階次不及，除錄事參軍、襄威將軍，帶長安令。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Yuan Chang went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province and requested Jing as his chief of staff; because Jing's rank was insufficient, he was appointed Recorder and Staff Officer, General Who Displays Might, and concurrently Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chang of the Secretariat went out as General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Yong, he asked for Jing as chief of staff; because Jing's rank was too low, he was named Recorder and Staff Officer and General Who Displays Might, with concurrent duties as magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 甚有惠政，民吏稱之。

translations.literal: He had very benevolent administration; the people and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was notably benevolent, and people and officials alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常劉芳與景等撰朝令，未及班行。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang together with Jing and others had compiled court ordinances, but they had not yet been promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang had worked with Jing and others on court ordinances that had not yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 別典儀注，多所草創，未成，芳卒，景纂成其事。

translations.literal: Separate canonical ritual regulations had largely been drafted but not completed; when Fang died, Jing compiled and finished the work.
translations.idiomatic: Separate ritual codes had been largely drafted but left unfinished; when Fang died, Jing completed the compilation.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，召景赴京，還修儀注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, Jing was summoned to the capital and returned to revise the ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Jing was recalled to the capital to resume work on the ritual codes.

sentences.zh: 拜謁者僕射，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Messengers and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Messengers with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 又以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrent Palace Secretariat Attendant in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made concurrent Palace Secretariat Attendant while retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 後授步兵校尉，仍舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was given the post of Commandant of Footsoldiers, still serving as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers while continuing as attendant.

sentences.zh: 又敕撰太和之後朝儀已施行者，凡五十餘卷。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to compile court ceremonies put into practice after the Taihe era, more than fifty volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to compile court ceremonies enacted after the Taihe era, more than fifty volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后詔依漢世陰鄧二后故事，親奉廟祀，與帝交獻。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict following the precedent of the two empresses Yin and Deng of Han, personally conducting temple sacrifices and exchanging offerings with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling then ordered ritual following the Han precedents of Empresses Yin and Deng, whereby she would personally conduct temple sacrifices and exchange offerings with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 景乃據正，以定儀注，朝廷是之。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon relied on what was correct to fix the ritual regulations, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jing appealed to canonical precedent to fix the ritual regulations, and the court approved his ruling.

sentences.zh: 正光初，除龍驤將軍、中散大夫，舍人如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengguang era he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and Grand Master of Palace Discourse, his attendant post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengguang era he was named General of the Dragon Cavalry and Grand Master of Palace Discourse while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 時肅宗行講學之禮於國子寺，[5]司徒崔光執經，敕景與董紹、張徹、馮元興、王延業、鄭伯猷等俱為錄義。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Suzong performed the lecture rite at the Imperial University; [5] Minister of Works Cui Guang held the classic, and Jing together with Dong Shao, Zhang Che, Feng Yuanxing, Wang Yanye, Zheng Boyou, and others were all ordered to record the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming held the lecture rite at the Imperial University, [5] Minister of Works Cui Guang expounded the classic, and Jing was ordered together with Dong Shao, Zhang Che, Feng Yuanxing, Wang Yanye, and Zheng Boyou to record the interpretation.

sentences.zh: 事畢，又行釋奠之禮，並詔百官作釋奠詩，時以景作為美。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, the libation rite was also performed, and all officials were ordered to compose libation poems; at the time Jing's composition was judged the finest.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, the libation ceremony was performed as well, and all officials were ordered to compose libation poems; Jing's piece was judged the finest.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，蠕蠕主阿那瓌歸闕，朝廷疑其位次。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year the Rouran ruler Anagui returned to court, and the court doubted his precedence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year the Rouran ruler Anagui came to court, and the court debated his ceremonial precedence.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍訪景，景曰：「昔咸寧中，南單于來朝，晉世處之王公、特進之下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gaoyang Yong consulted Jing; Jing said, "In former times during the Xianning era, when the Southern Chanyu came to court, the Jin age placed him below princes and dukes and special advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang consulted Jing, who said, "In the Xianning era, when the Southern Chanyu came to court, the Jin placed him below princes and dukes and holders of special advance.

sentences.zh: 今日為班，宜在蕃王、儀同三司之間。」

translations.literal: For today's seating, he should be placed between foreign princes and Holders of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: For today's seating he should rank between foreign princes and Holders of Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 雍從之。

translations.literal: Yong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yong followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 朝廷典章，疑而不決，則時訪景而行。

translations.literal: Whenever court statutes and regulations were doubtful and unresolved, the court would consult Jing and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court ritual or statute was in doubt, the court would consult Jing and follow his ruling.

sentences.zh: 初，平齊之後，光祿大夫高聰徙於北京，中書監高允為之娉妻，給其資宅。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the pacification of Qi, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Gao Cong was moved to the Northern Capital; Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Yun arranged a wife for him and supplied him with a residence and goods.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Qi, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Gao Cong was transferred to the Northern Capital; Gao Yun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, arranged his marriage and provided him a house and stipend.

sentences.zh: 聰後為允立碑，每云：「吾以此文報德，足矣。」

translations.literal: Later Cong erected a stele for Yun and often said, "With this text I repay his virtue—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Cong later erected a stele for Yun and would say, "With this inscription I have repaid his kindness—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史常綽以未盡其美。

translations.literal: The Governor of Yu Province Chang Chuo held that it did not exhaust his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chang Chuo of Yu Province felt it did not do justice to Yun's virtues.

sentences.zh: 景尚允才器，先為遺德頌，司徒崔光聞而觀之，尋味良久，乃云：「高光祿平日每矜其文，自許報允之德，今見常生此頌，高氏不得獨擅其美也。」

translations.literal: Jing admired Yun's talent and capacity and had first composed a eulogy of his remaining virtue; Minister of Works Cui Guang heard of it and read it, savoring it for a long while, then said, "Master Gao the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness usually prides himself on his writing and considers himself to have repaid Yun's virtue; now seeing Master Chang's eulogy, the Gao family cannot monopolize the praise."
translations.idiomatic: Jing admired Yun's gifts and had already written a eulogy of his virtues; when Minister of Works Cui Guang read it he pondered it at length and said, "Gao Cong has always prided himself on his prose and claimed he had repaid Yun's kindness; now that Chang Jing has written this eulogy, the Gao family can no longer claim the credit alone."

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光、安豐王延明受詔議定服章，敕景參修其事。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and the Prince of Anfeng Yanming received an edict to deliberate and fix dress and insignia; Jing was ordered to participate in revising the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang and Prince Yanming of Anfeng were ordered to fix court dress and insignia, and Jing was directed to assist.

sentences.zh: 尋進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long his title was advanced to General Who Wins the Championship.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Wins the Championship.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓌之還國也，境上遷延，仍陳窘乏。

translations.literal: When Anagui returned to his state, he lingered at the border and again reported distress and shortage.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui returned home he lingered at the frontier and again pleaded poverty and want.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書左丞元孚奉詔振恤，阿那瓌執孚過柔玄，奔于漠北。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Fu was sent with an edict to bring relief; Anagui seized Fu and took him past Rouxuan, fleeing to the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yuan Fu was sent with an edict to bring relief; Anagui seized him, carried him past Rouxuan, and fled into the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書令李崇、御史中尉兼右僕射元纂追討，不及。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Chong and Censor-in-Chief concurrently Right Vice Director Yuan Zuan were sent in pursuit but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chong and Censor-in-Chief Yuan Zuan, who was also Right Vice Director, were sent in pursuit but failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 乃令景出塞，經瓫山，臨瀚海，宣敕勒眾而返。

translations.literal: Jing was then ordered to go beyond the frontier, pass Mount Pi, come to the Hanhai Sea, proclaim the edict and restrain the host, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was then ordered beyond the frontier; he passed Mount Pi, reached the Hanhai, proclaimed the edict to restrain the troops, and returned.

sentences.zh: 景經涉山水，悵然懷古，乃擬劉琨扶風歌十二首。

translations.literal: As Jing traveled through mountains and rivers he grew melancholy with thoughts of antiquity and composed twelve pieces in imitation of Liu Kun's Songs of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through mountains and rivers, Jing grew wistful for the past and wrote twelve poems in the manner of Liu Kun's Songs of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he was made concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Service Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era he was appointed concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Service Section.

sentences.zh: 尋除左將軍、太府少卿，仍舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Left General and Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse, still serving as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was named Left General and Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 固辭少卿不拜，改授散騎常侍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the vice ministership and did not accept it; he was instead given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the vice ministership; he was instead appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while keeping his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史元法僧叛入蕭衍，衍遣其豫章王蕭綜入據彭城。

translations.literal: Governor of Xu Province Yuan Faseng rebelled and went over to Xiao Yan; Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong to enter and hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng, governor of Xu Province, defected to Liang emperor Xiao Yan, who sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Zong, to seize Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時安豐王延明為大都督、大行臺，率臨淮王彧等眾軍討之。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Anfeng Yanming was Grand Commander and Grand Mobile Commandery, leading the Prince of Linhuai Yu and other armies to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yanming of Anfeng served as Grand Commander and head of the grand mobile headquarters, leading Prince Yu of Linhuai and other forces against them.

sentences.zh: 既而蕭綜降附，徐州清復，遣景兼尚書，持節馳與行臺、都督觀機部分。

translations.literal: Before long Xiao Zong surrendered and submitted; Xu Province was cleared and restored; Jing was sent as concurrent Director of the Secretariat, bearing the staff of authority to hurry to the mobile commandery and the commander to observe circumstances and assign forces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zong soon surrendered; Xu Province was restored, and Jing was sent as concurrent Director of the Secretariat with credentials to join the mobile headquarters and commander and assign forces as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 景經洛汭，乃作銘焉。

translations.literal: When Jing passed the bend of the Luo River he composed an inscription there.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the bend of the Luo, he composed an inscription.

sentences.zh: 是時，尚書令蕭寶夤，都督崔延伯，都督、北海王顥，都督、車騎將軍元恒芝等並各出討，詔景詣軍宣旨勞問。

translations.literal: At that time Director of the Secretariat Xiao Baoyin, Commander Cui Yanbo, Commander the Prince of Beihai Hao, Commander General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuan Hengzhi, and others each went out on campaign; an edict ordered Jing to go to the armies to proclaim the imperial will and offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Director Xiao Baoyin, Commander Cui Yanbo, Commander Prince Hao of Beihai, and Commander General of Chariots and Cavalry Yuan Hengzhi were each campaigning; Jing was ordered to visit the armies and convey the emperor's greetings.

sentences.zh: 還，以本將軍授徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On his return he was given his original general's title and appointed Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed governor of Xu Province while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 杜洛周反於燕州，仍以景兼尚書為行臺，與幽州都督、平北將軍元譚以禦之。

translations.literal: When Du Luozhou rebelled in Yan Province, Jing was again made concurrent Director of the Secretariat as mobile commandery, together with Commander of You Province General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Tan, to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Luozhou rebelled in Yan Province, Jing was again made concurrent Director of the Secretariat on the mobile headquarters, together with Commander Yuan Tan of You Province, General Who Pacifies the North, to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 景表求勒幽州諸縣悉入古城，山路有通賊之處，權發兵夫，隨宜置戍，以為防遏。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized requesting that all counties of You Province be urged into old walled cities; wherever mountain roads gave access to bandits, labor and troops should be dispatched as expedient to set garrisons for defense and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized that every county in You Province should withdraw into old walled towns; wherever mountain paths gave bandits access, troops should be levied as needed to establish garrisons for defense.

sentences.zh: 又以頃來差兵，不盡強壯，今之三長，皆是豪門多丁為之，今求權發為兵。

translations.literal: He also noted that in recent conscription not all men levied were strong and robust; the present Three Chiefs were all drawn from wealthy clans with many sons, and he now requested permission to conscript them as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He also observed that recent levies had not produced enough able-bodied men: the Three Chiefs were all wealthy households with many sons, and he now asked leave to draft them for military service.

sentences.zh: 肅宗皆從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: Jing was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 別敕譚西至軍都關，北從盧龍塞，據此二嶮，以杜賊出入之路。

translations.literal: A separate edict ordered Tan west to Jundu Pass and north through the Lulong Barrier, to hold these two defiles and block the rebels' routes in and out.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict ordered Tan west to Jundu Pass and north through the Lulong Barrier, holding those two defiles to cut the rebels' lines of advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 又詔景山中嶮路之處，悉令捍塞。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Jing to block and seal every perilous route through the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was also ordered to fortify and block every dangerous mountain pass.

sentences.zh: 景遣府錄事參軍裴智成發范陽三長之兵以守白㠈，都督元譚據居庸下口。

translations.literal: Jing dispatched Registrar of the Secretariat Pei Zhicheng to levy the militia of the Three Chiefs of Fanyang to hold Bai'ao Pass, while Commander Yuan Tan held the lower outlet of Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his registrar Pei Zhicheng to raise the Fanyang militia and hold Bai'ao (White Cliff) Pass, while Commander Yuan Tan took the lower outlet of Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 俄而安州石離、冗城、斛鹽三戍兵反，[6]結洛周，有眾二萬餘落，自松岍赴賊。

translations.literal: Soon the garrison troops at Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province rebelled, joined Luozhou, mustered more than twenty thousand households, and marched from Songqian to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the garrisons at Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province mutinied, rallied to Luozhou, and with more than twenty thousand households marched from Songqian to join the rebels.

sentences.zh: [7]譚勒別將崔仲哲等截軍都關以待之。

translations.literal: Tan led detached generals Cui Zhongzhe and others to intercept at Jundu Pass and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan led detached generals including Cui Zhongzhe to block Jundu Pass and await them.

sentences.zh: 仲哲戰沒，洛周又自外應之，腹背受敵，譚遂大敗，諸軍夜散。

translations.literal: Zhongzhe died in battle; Luozhou also supported from outside; caught between enemies front and rear, Tan suffered a great defeat and the armies dispersed by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhe fell in battle; Luozhou attacked from outside as well, and Tan, caught between two forces, was routed and his troops scattered overnight.

sentences.zh: 詔以景所部別將李琚為都督，代譚征下口，降景為後將軍，解州任，仍詔景為幽安玄□四州行臺。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li Ju, a detached general under Jing, as commander to replace Tan at the lower pass; Jing was demoted to Rear General and relieved of provincial duties, yet was still appointed mobile headquarters for the four provinces of You, An, Xuan, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Li Ju, a detached general under Jing, commander in Tan's place at the lower pass; Jing was demoted to Rear General and stripped of his provincial post, but was still named head of the mobile headquarters for You, An, Xuan, and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 賊既南出，鈔掠薊城，景命統軍梁仲禮率兵士邀擊，破之，獲賊將禦夷鎮軍主孫念恒。

translations.literal: Once the rebels moved south and raided Ji city, Jing ordered Commandant Liang Zhongli to lead troops in intercepting attack, defeated them, and captured the rebel general Defender of Yuyi Sun Nianheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels pushed south and plundered Ji, Jing ordered Commandant Liang Zhongli to intercept them; Liang routed the force and captured the rebel general Sun Nianheng, garrison commander of Yuyi.

sentences.zh: 都督李琚為賊所攻，薊城之北軍敗而死。

translations.literal: Commander Li Ju was attacked by rebels and died in defeat north of Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Ju was attacked by the rebels and killed north of Ji in a losing battle.

sentences.zh: 率屬城人禦之，[8]賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jing led the people of subordinate cities to resist them, and the rebels dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the people of the outlying towns to defend Ji, and the rebels did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 洛周還據上谷。

translations.literal: Luozhou withdrew and held Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou withdrew and reoccupied Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 授景平北將軍、光祿大夫，行臺如故。

translations.literal: Jing was given the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendor, his mobile headquarters unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendor, retaining his mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 洛周遣其都督王曹紇真、馬叱斤等率眾薊南，以掠人穀，乃遇連雨，賊眾疲勞。

translations.literal: Luozhou sent his commanders Wang, Cao Hezhen, Ma Chijin, and others to lead troops south of Ji to plunder grain; they then encountered continuous rain and the rebel force grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou sent commanders including Wang, Cao Hezhen, and Ma Chijin south of Ji to seize grain, but unseasonable rains exhausted his troops.

sentences.zh: 景與都督于榮、刺史王延年置兵粟園。

translations.literal: Jing together with Commander Yu Rong and Governor Wang Yannian set troops at Mil Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Commander Yu Rong, and Governor Wang Yannian deployed troops at Mil Garden.

sentences.zh: [9]邀其走路，大敗之，斬曹紇真。

translations.literal: They intercepted the rebels' line of retreat, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded Cao Hezhen.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off the rebels' retreat, routed them, and killed Cao Hezhen.

sentences.zh: 洛周率眾南趨范陽，景與延年及榮復破之。

translations.literal: Luozhou led his force south toward Fanyang; Jing together with Yannian and Rong again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou marched south on Fanyang, but Jing, Yannian, and Rong defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 又遣別將重破之於州西虎眼泉，擒斬及溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: He also sent a detached general who again defeated them at Tiger Eye Spring west of the province; captured, killed, and drowned dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: A detached force under his command routed them again at Tiger Eye Spring west of the province, killing or drowning a great number.

sentences.zh: 後洛周南圍范陽，城人翻降，執刺史延年及景送於洛周。

translations.literal: Later Luozhou besieged Fanyang from the south; the townspeople turned and surrendered, seized Governor Yannian and Jing, and delivered them to Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou later besieged Fanyang from the south; the townspeople rebelled, seized Governors Yannian and Jing, and handed them over to Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 洛周尋為葛榮所吞，景又入榮。

translations.literal: Luozhou was soon absorbed by Ge Rong, and Jing also entered Ge Rong's service.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou was soon swallowed up by Ge Rong, and Jing entered Ge Rong's camp as well.

sentences.zh: 榮破，景得還朝。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was defeated, Jing was able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat, Jing returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 永安初，詔復本官，兼黃門侍郎，又攝著作，固辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era an edict restored his original office, with concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and also acting Compiler of Documents; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yong'an era he was ordered back to his former post with concurrent service as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and acting Compiler of Documents, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 二年，除中軍將軍，正黃門。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made General of the Central Army with regular status as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed General of the Central Army and regular Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，參議正光壬子曆，至是賜爵高陽子。

translations.literal: Earlier he had participated in deliberating the Zhengguang renchen calendar; at this time he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier helped revise the Zhengguang renchen calendar; now he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 元顥內逼，莊帝北巡，景與侍中、大司馬、安豐王延明在禁中召諸親賓，安慰京師。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang went on a northern tour; Jing together with Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, Prince of Anfeng Yanming summoned kinsmen and guests within the Forbidden City to reassure the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao threatened the capital, Emperor Zhuang withdrew north; Jing joined Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Prince Yanming of Anfeng in summoning kinsmen and guests inside the palace to steady the city.

sentences.zh: 顥入洛，景仍居本位。

translations.literal: When Hao entered Luoyang, Jing remained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao took Luoyang, Jing kept his existing office.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，解黃門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Jing was relieved of the Yellow Gate post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Jing was removed from the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除車騎將軍、右光祿大夫、祕書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Putai era he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Grand Master of Splendor, and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Putai era he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Grand Master of Splendor, and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以預詔命之勤，封濮陽縣子。

translations.literal: For his diligence in drafting edicts, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puyang County.
translations.idiomatic: For his work drafting imperial edicts, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puyang County.

sentences.zh: 後以例追。

translations.literal: Later the enfeoffment was revoked under precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The title was later revoked under the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，監議事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he supervised deliberations on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he oversaw deliberations on state business.

sentences.zh: 景自少及老，恒居事任。

translations.literal: From youth to old age Jing always held responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Jing was always in active service.

sentences.zh: 清儉自守，不營產業，至於衣食，取濟而已。

translations.literal: Pure and frugal in self-restraint, he did not manage estates; as for food and clothing, he took only enough to get by.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and frugally, built no fortune, and took from his income no more than he needed for food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 耽好經史，愛玩文詞，若遇新異之書，殷勤求訪，或復質買，不問價之貴賤，必以得為期。

translations.literal: He was devoted to the classics and histories and delighted in literary phrasing; when he encountered new or unusual books he sought them eagerly, sometimes pawning things to buy them, regardless of price, resolved to obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics and histories and delighted in fine writing; whenever he found a new or unusual book he hunted it down, even pawning belongings to buy it, caring nothing for the price so long as he could possess it.

sentences.zh: 友人刁整每謂曰：「卿清德自居，不事家業，雖儉約可尚，將何以自濟也？

translations.literal: His friend Diao Zheng often said to him: "You maintain pure virtue and do not attend to family livelihood; though frugality is admirable, how will you support yourself?
translations.idiomatic: His friend Diao Zheng often told him, "You hold yourself to pure conduct and keep no household estate; frugality is admirable, but how will you live?

sentences.zh: 吾恐摯太常方餧於栢谷耳。」

translations.literal: I fear you will end up like Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhi starving in Baigu Valley."
