translations.idiomatic: I fear you will go the way of Grand Master Zhi, starving in Baigu Valley."

sentences.zh: 遂與衞將軍羊深矜其所乏，乃率刁雙、司馬彥邕、李諧、畢祖彥、畢義顯等各出錢千文而為買馬焉。

translations.literal: So together with Palace Guard General Yang Shen, sympathizing with his want, they led Diao Shuang, Sima Yanrong, Li Xie, Bi Zuyan, Bi Yixian, and others each to contribute a thousand coins and buy him a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen, General of the Palace Guard, took pity on his poverty and, with Diao Shuang, Sima Yanrong, Li Xie, Bi Zuyan, Bi Yixian, and others, each contributed a thousand coins and bought him a horse.

sentences.zh: 景善與人交，終始若一，其遊處者，皆服其深遠之度，未曾見其矜吝之心。

translations.literal: Jing was skilled at friendship, consistent from beginning to end; those who associated with him all admired the depth and distance of his measure, and never saw a stingy heart in him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made friends easily and kept them faithfully; those who knew him admired his depth of character and never saw a trace of meanness in him.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，澹於榮利，自得懷抱，不事權門。

translations.literal: He loved drinking wine, was indifferent to glory and profit, content in his own mind, and did not court powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed wine, cared little for rank and gain, was at peace within himself, and never cultivated the great houses.

sentences.zh: 性和厚恭慎。

translations.literal: His nature was mild, generous, and reverently cautious.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament was gentle, generous, and reverently cautious.

sentences.zh: 每讀書，見韋弦之事，深薄之危，乃圖古昔可以鑒戒，指事為象，讚而述之曰：

translations.literal: Whenever he read and saw matters of bowstring admonition and the peril of leaning too deep, he would depict ancient precedents that could serve as mirrors and warnings, pointing to events as images, and praise and narrate them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read of the bowstring's warning or the danger of leaning too far, he would draw on ancient examples that might serve as cautionary mirrors, take events as emblems, and compose a laudatory account, saying:

sentences.zh: 周雅云：「謂天蓋高，不敢不跼；

translations.literal: The Zhou Odes say: "They say Heaven covers high—I dare not but crouch;
translations.idiomatic: The Odes of Zhou say: "Heaven is said to vault high—I dare not but bow low;

sentences.zh: 謂地蓋厚，不敢不蹐。」

translations.literal: They say Earth lies deep—I dare not but tread lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Earth is said to lie deep—I dare not but step with care."

sentences.zh: 有朝隱大夫監戒斯文，乃惕焉而懼曰：「夫道喪則性傾，利重則身輕。

translations.literal: A Hidden-in-Court Grandee supervised and warned over this text, and in fear and caution said: "When the Way is lost the nature inclines; when profit weighs heavy the person grows light.
translations.idiomatic: A court recluse supervised this text as a warning and said in trembling dread: "When the Way is lost, character topples; when profit weighs heavy, the self grows light.

sentences.zh: 是故乘和體遜，式銘方冊；

translations.literal: Therefore to embrace harmony and embody humility, inscribe it on tablets;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore embrace harmony and embody humility—inscribe them on the tablets of record;

sentences.zh: 防微慎獨，載象丹青。

translations.literal: to guard against the subtle and be careful in solitude, depict it in vermilion and blue.
translations.idiomatic: guard against the subtle and be watchful in solitude—paint them in red and blue.

sentences.zh: 信哉辭人之賦，文晦而理明。

translations.literal: Truly the poet's rhapsody—words obscure yet principle clear.
translations.idiomatic: How true the poet's rhapsody: the wording is veiled, yet the principle shines clear.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻高天，聽卑視諦；

translations.literal: Gazing up at lofty Heaven, listening low and seeing clearly;
translations.idiomatic: Look up at lofty Heaven—it listens below and sees with clarity;

sentences.zh: 俯測厚地，岳峻川渟。

translations.literal: Looking down to measure deep Earth—peaks steep, rivers still.
translations.idiomatic: Look down upon deep Earth—its peaks rise steep, its rivers lie still.

sentences.zh: 誰其戴之，不私不畏。

translations.literal: Who bears it aloft? Without partiality, without dread.
translations.idiomatic: Who bears it up? Neither partial nor fearful.

sentences.zh: 誰其踐之，不陷不墜。

translations.literal: Who treads upon it? Without sinking, without falling.
translations.idiomatic: Who treads upon it? Neither sinking nor falling.

sentences.zh: 故善惡是徵，物罔同異。

translations.literal: Thus good and evil are the proof—things are not all alike.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil are thereby revealed—things are not all the same.

sentences.zh: 論亢匪久，人咸敬忌。

translations.literal: To reach the heights is not for long—all men alike revere and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Exalted standing does not last—every man alike holds it in reverence and dread.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 唯地厚矣，尚亦兢兢。

translations.literal: Though Earth is so deep, still one must be tremblingly cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Though Earth is deep beyond measure, still one must walk in trembling care.

sentences.zh: 浩浩名位，孰識其親。

translations.literal: Vast name and rank—who knows their kin?
translations.idiomatic: Rank and title spread vast—who can grasp their true nature?

sentences.zh: 搏之弗得，聆之無聞。

translations.literal: Grasp them—you cannot; listen—you hear nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Grasp them—you cannot hold them; listen—you hear nothing.

sentences.zh: 故有戒於顯而急乎微。

translations.literal: Hence there is warning in the manifest and urgency in the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Hence warning lies in what is plain, and urgency in what is slight.

sentences.zh: 好爵是冒，聲奢是基。

translations.literal: Noble rank is what one dares seize; lavish renown is what one dares build upon.
translations.idiomatic: Men dare to grasp fine rank; they dare to build on lavish fame.

sentences.zh: 身陷於祿利，言溺於是非。

translations.literal: The body sinks in salary and profit; words drown in right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The body sinks in salary and gain; speech drowns in dispute.

sentences.zh: 或求欲而未厭，或知足而不辭。

translations.literal: Some seek desires and are never sated; some know sufficiency yet do not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Some chase desire and never have enough; some know when they have enough yet will not step back.

sentences.zh: 是故位高而勢愈迫，正立而邪愈欺。

translations.literal: Therefore the higher the rank the fiercer the pressure; stand upright and evil presses more to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the higher the rank, the fiercer the pressure; stand upright, and wickedness presses harder to deceive.

sentences.zh: 安有位極而危不萃，邪榮而正不凋。

translations.literal: How could one reach the pinnacle without peril gathering, or honor wickedness without the upright withering?
translations.idiomatic: Can anyone reach the summit without peril gathering, or exalt wickedness without the upright withering?

sentences.zh: 故悔多於地厚，禍甚於天高。

translations.literal: Thus regret is more than Earth's depth; calamity greater than Heaven's height.
translations.idiomatic: Regret runs deeper than Earth; calamity rises higher than Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夫悔未結，誰肯曲躬？

translations.literal: Before regret is knit, who will bow the body?
translations.idiomatic: Before regret has taken hold, who will bow low?

sentences.zh: 夫禍未加，誰肯累足？

translations.literal: Before calamity falls, who will tread with gathered feet?
translations.idiomatic: Before disaster strikes, who will walk with gathered steps?

sentences.zh: 固機發而後思圖，車覆而後改躅。

translations.literal: Only after the trigger is pulled does one think to plot; only after the cart overturns does one change step.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the bolt is loosed does one think to plan; only after the cart overturns does one change stride.

sentences.zh: 改之無及，故狡兔失穴；

translations.literal: Too late to change—hence the cunning hare loses its burrow;
translations.idiomatic: Too late to mend—thus the cunning hare loses its burrow;

sentences.zh: 思之在後，故逆鱗易觸。

translations.literal: To think only afterward—hence the inverted scales are easily touched.
translations.idiomatic: To think only afterward—thus the dragon's scales are easily provoked.

sentences.zh: 君子則不然，體舒則懷卷，視溺則思濟。

translations.literal: The gentleman is not so; when at ease he holds the scroll, when he sees one drowning he thinks to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman is otherwise: at ease he keeps the classic scroll in mind; seeing one drowning, he thinks to save him.

sentences.zh: 原夫人□之度，[10]𨗿於無階之天；

translations.literal: By the measure of the human heart, one surpasses the ladderless Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: By the measure of the human heart, one transcends Heaven without steps;

sentences.zh: 勢位之危，深於不測之地。

translations.literal: the peril of status and rank is deeper than untraveled ground.
translations.idiomatic: the peril of power and rank runs deeper than unfathomed ground.

sentences.zh: 餌厚而躬不競，爵降而心不係。

translations.literal: Though bait is rich the body does not contend; though rank falls the heart is not bound.
translations.idiomatic: Though the bait is rich, the body does not strive; though rank falls, the heart is not tethered.

sentences.zh: 守善於已成，懼愆於未敗。

translations.literal: One keeps goodness when success is already achieved; fears fault before ruin has come.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps to virtue when success is already won; he fears fault before ruin arrives.

sentences.zh: 雖盈而戒沖，通而慮滯。

translations.literal: Though full, one guards emptiness; though unimpeded, one considers stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Though full, he guards against excess; though unimpeded, he considers stagnation.

sentences.zh: 以知命為遐齡，以樂天為大惠，以戢智而從時，以懷愚而遊世。

translations.literal: To take knowing fate as long life, taking joy in Heaven as great grace, to sheathe wisdom and follow the time, to embrace simplicity and wander the world.
translations.idiomatic: He takes knowing fate as long life, joy in Heaven as the greatest blessing, sheathes wisdom and follows the age, and embraces simplicity as he moves through the world.

sentences.zh: 曲躬焉，累足焉。

translations.literal: Bow the body; gather the feet.
translations.idiomatic: He bows his body; he gathers his steps.

sentences.zh: 苟行之晝已決矣，猶夜則思其計。

translations.literal: Though the day's course is already decided, still at night one thinks through the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Though the day's course is already settled, at night he still weighs the plan.

sentences.zh: 誦之口亦明矣，故心必賞其契。

translations.literal: Though the mouth recites it clearly, therefore the heart must prize the accord.
translations.idiomatic: Though the mouth recites it plainly, the heart must prize the truth it holds.

sentences.zh: 故能不同不誘，而弭謗於羣小；

translations.literal: Thus he can neither conform nor be enticed, and still quell slander among petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Thus he need neither conform nor be enticed, yet still quells slander among petty men;

sentences.zh: 無毀無譽，而貽信於上帝。

translations.literal: without ruin, without praise, yet leave trust with High Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: without ruin or renown, yet leave trust with High Heaven.

sentences.zh: 託身與金石俱堅，立名與天壤相弊。

translations.literal: Entrust the body to stand firm as metal and stone; establish a name to decay with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusts his person to stand firm as metal and stone; he establishes a name to endure until Heaven and Earth wear away.

sentences.zh: 囂競無侵，優遊獨逝。

translations.literal: No clamorous rivalry invades; at leisure he goes alone.
translations.idiomatic: No clamorous rivalry touches him; at ease he passes on alone.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，故綺閣金門，可安其宅；

translations.literal: If it is so, then brocade pavilions and golden gates can shelter his dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, then brocade halls and golden gates may shelter his home;

sentences.zh: 錦衣玉食，可頤其形。

translations.literal: brocade robes and jade fare can nourish his form.
translations.idiomatic: brocade robes and jade fare may nourish his person.

sentences.zh: 柳下三黜，不慍其色；

translations.literal: Three dismissals of Liuxia—and no anger on his face;
translations.idiomatic: Three dismissals of Liuxia Hui—and no anger on his face;

sentences.zh: 子文三陟，不喜其情。

translations.literal: Three promotions of Ziwen—and no joy in his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Three promotions of Ziwen—and no joy in his countenance.

sentences.zh: 而惑者見居高可以持勢，欲乘高以據榮。

translations.literal: But the confused, seeing that height can hold power, wish to ride height to seize glory.
translations.idiomatic: But the deluded, seeing that height can hold power, wish to climb high and seize glory.

sentences.zh: 見直道可以修己，欲專道以邀聲。

translations.literal: Seeing that the straight Way can cultivate the self, they wish to monopolize the Way to invite renown.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the straight Way can refine the self, they wish to monopolize the Way and court fame.

sentences.zh: 夫去聲，然後聲可立，豈矜道之所宣。

translations.literal: Only after renouncing renown can renown be established—how could one boast of what the Way proclaims?
translations.idiomatic: Only by renouncing fame can fame be established—how could one boast of what the Way proclaims?

sentences.zh: 慮危，然後安可固，豈假道之所全。

translations.literal: Only after considering peril can safety be secured—how could one borrow the Way for completeness?
translations.idiomatic: Only by reckoning with peril can safety be secured—how could one borrow the Way to preserve oneself whole?

sentences.zh: 是以君子鑒恃道不可以流聲，故去聲而懷道；

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman reflects that relying on the Way cannot float renown, and so renounces renown and embraces the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the gentleman sees that leaning on the Way cannot spread one's fame, and so renounces fame and holds to the Way;

sentences.zh: 鑒專道不可以守勢，故去勢以崇道。

translations.literal: reflects that monopolizing the Way cannot guard power, and so renounces power to exalt the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He sees that monopolizing the Way cannot guard power, and so renounces power to exalt the Way.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 履道雖高，不得無亢；

translations.literal: Though one treads the Way high, one cannot be without excess;
translations.idiomatic: Though one walks the Way on high, one cannot be without excess;

sentences.zh: 求聲雖道，不得無悔。

translations.literal: Though one seeks renown by the Way, one cannot be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though one seeks fame by the Way, one cannot be without regret.

sentences.zh: 然則聲奢繁則實儉凋；

translations.literal: Then when renown grows lavish and elaborate, substance and thrift wither;
translations.idiomatic: When fame grows lavish and elaborate, substance and restraint wither;

sentences.zh: 功業進則身迹退。

translations.literal: when merit and achievement advance, bodily traces retreat.
translations.idiomatic: when merit and achievement advance, the person himself recedes.

sentences.zh: 如此，則精靈遂越，驕侈自親。

translations.literal: Thus, then the spirit crosses over, and arrogance and extravagance draw near of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When this happens, the inner spirit slips away and arrogance and extravagance take hold.

sentences.zh: 情與道絕，事與勢隣。

translations.literal: Feelings are cut off from the Way, and affairs border on power.
translations.idiomatic: The heart is severed from the Way, and one's affairs cling to power.

sentences.zh: 方欲役思以持勢，乘勢以求津。

translations.literal: Just as one would deploy thought to maintain power and ride power to seek the ford.
translations.idiomatic: Just as one sets the mind to harness power and rides power to find a way forward,

sentences.zh: 故利欲誘其情，禍難嬰其身。

translations.literal: Therefore profit and desire seduce one's feelings, and disaster and hardship afflict one's person.
translations.idiomatic: profit and desire seduce the heart, and calamity and disaster close in on the person.

sentences.zh: 利欲交，則幽明以之變；

translations.literal: When profit and desire intertwine, then the dark and bright realms change thereby;
translations.idiomatic: When profit and desire entwine, the realms of the living and the dead are overturned;

sentences.zh: 禍難構，則智術無所陳。

translations.literal: When disaster and hardship take shape, then wisdom and stratagem have nowhere to be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: when calamity and disaster take shape, wisdom and stratagem have nowhere to be deployed.

sentences.zh: 若然者，雖縻爵帝扃，焉得而寧之？

translations.literal: If it is so, even though one is bound by noble rank at the emperor's gate, how can one thereby find peace?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, though one be shackled to noble rank at the emperor's gate, how could one find peace?

sentences.zh: 雖結珮皇庭，焉得而榮之？

translations.literal: Even though one wears jade pendants in the imperial court, how can one thereby find glory?
translations.idiomatic: Though one wear jade pendants in the imperial court, how could one find glory in it?

sentences.zh: 故身道未究，而崇邪之徑已形。

translations.literal: Therefore the personal Way is not yet fully pursued, but the path that exalts perversity has already taken form.
translations.idiomatic: Before the way of self-cultivation is fully pursued, the path of exalting perversity has already appeared.

sentences.zh: 成功未立，而修正之術已生。

translations.literal: Success is not yet established, but the art of correction has already been born.
translations.idiomatic: Before success is established, the means of correction have already sprung up.

sentences.zh: 福祿交蹇於人事，屯難頓萃於時情。

translations.literal: Fortune and emolument together meet obstruction in human affairs, and hardship suddenly gathers in the temper of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and rank meet obstruction in human affairs, and hardship suddenly gathers in the temper of the times.

sentences.zh: 忠介剖心於白日，耿節沉骨於幽靈。

translations.literal: The loyal and upright lay open their hearts under the white sun, and steadfast integrity sinks its bones among the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal lay open their hearts under the bright sun, while upright integrity is buried among the shades.

sentences.zh: 因斯愚智之所機，倚伏之所係，全亡之所依，其在遜順而已哉。

translations.literal: Because of this—what fools and sages hinge upon, what rise and fall depend on, what preservation and destruction rely on—it lies in yielding and compliance alone!
translations.idiomatic: On this depend what fools and sages alike stake their fate, what rise and fall hang upon, and what preservation and destruction rest upon—surely it lies in yielding and compliance alone!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼鑒之！

translations.literal: Alas—take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Ah—take this as a warning!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼鑒之！

translations.literal: Alas—take this as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Ah—take this as a warning!

sentences.zh: 景所著述數百篇，見行於世，刪正晉司空張華博物志及撰儒林、列女傳各數十篇云。

translations.literal: Jing's compositions numbered several hundred pieces circulating in the world; he edited and corrected the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Bowuzhi and compiled several dozen chapters each of the Rulin and Lienv Zhuan, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's writings numbered several hundred pieces in circulation; he revised the Jin Grand Marshal Zhang Hua's Records of Broad Learning and is said to have compiled several dozen chapters each of Biographies of Confucian Scholars and Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 長子昶，少學識，有文才。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chang, from youth learned and knowledgeable, possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chang was learned from youth and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 昶弟彪之，永安中，司空行參軍。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Biaozhi, during the Yong'an era, served as Acting Staff Member under the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Biaozhi served as Acting Staff Member under the Grand Marshal during the Yong'an era.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：琰之好學博聞，鬱為邦彥。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yan Zhi loved learning and was widely informed, flourishing as a leading man of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yan Zhi loved learning and was widely informed, flourishing as a leading man of the state.

sentences.zh: 祖瑩幹能藝用，實曰時良。

translations.literal: Zu Ying's capability in talent and practical use truly made him a worthy man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ying's talent and practical ability truly made him a worthy man of the age.

sentences.zh: 常景以文義見宗，著美當代。

translations.literal: Chang Jing was honored for literary meaning and established renown in his own age.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing was honored for literary excellence and established a lasting reputation in his own age.

sentences.zh: 覽其遺稿，可稱尚哉。

translations.literal: Reading his surviving manuscripts, truly admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Reading his surviving manuscripts, one can only admire them.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十二 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本卷末有宋人校語云「魏收書列傳七十」，語未完，當脫「亡」字。

translations.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, juan 82 is marked "deficient." At the end of the Baibaina edition there is a Song-dynasty collation note reading "Wei Shou's book, Biographies seventy"; the sentence is incomplete and the character for "lost" is probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: The tables of contents in various editions of the Book of Wei mark juan 82 as deficient. At the end of the Baibaina edition a Song-dynasty collation note reads "Wei Shou's book, Biographies seventy"; the sentence is incomplete and the word "lost" is probably missing.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。」

translations.literal: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is deficient; later men supplied it.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is deficient; this was supplied by later hands.

sentences.zh: 按北史，祖瑩卷四七有傳，常景附卷四二常爽傳，李琰之見卷一００序傳。

translations.literal: According to the History of the Northern Dynasties, Zu Ying has a biography in juan 47; Chang Jing is appended to the biography of Chang Shuang in juan 42; Li Yan Zhi appears in the chronological biography in juan 100.
translations.idiomatic: According to the History of the Northern Dynasties, Zu Ying has a biography in juan 47; Chang Jing is appended to the biography of Chang Shuang in juan 42; and Li Yan Zhi appears in the chronological biography in juan 100.

sentences.zh: 檢此卷傳文大體與北史同，間有溢出語。

translations.literal: Examining the biographical texts in this volume, they largely agree with the History of the Northern Dynasties, though here and there are superfluous phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that the biographical texts in this volume largely agree with the History of the Northern Dynasties, though occasional stray phrases appear.

sentences.zh: 當是後人以北史相同諸人傳補，而增入高氏小史等他書中文句。

translations.literal: This should be a later restoration from the matching biographies in the History of the Northern Dynasties, with added passages from the Xiaoshi compiled by the Gao family and other books.
translations.idiomatic: This volume was likely restored by later hands from the matching biographies in the History of the Northern Dynasties, with added passages drawn from the Xiaoshi compiled by the Gao family and other works.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰辟為行臺參軍 北史卷一００序傳「臺」作「軍」。

translations.literal: Regarding "the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, recruited him as Acting Staff Member of the Mobile Headquarters": in the chronological biography in juan 100 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "tai" (headquarters) appears as "jun" (army).
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, recruited him as Acting Staff Member of the Mobile Headquarters": the chronological biography in juan 100 of the History of the Northern Dynasties reads "tai" (headquarters) as "jun" (army).

sentences.zh: 按彭城王勰未曾為行臺，且行臺屬僚皆同尚書省，不聞有參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, never served as head of a mobile headquarters, and the subordinates of a mobile headquarters all correspond to the Secretariat; one never hears of a staff member (canjun) among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, never served as head of a mobile headquarters, and the subordinates of a mobile headquarters all correspond to the Secretariat; there is no record of a staff member (canjun) among them.

sentences.zh: 但「行軍參軍」也罕見。

translations.literal: But "Acting Army Staff Member" is also rarely attested.
translations.idiomatic: But "Acting Army Staff Member" is also rarely attested.

sentences.zh: 「臺」或「軍」字或是衍文。

translations.literal: The character "tai" or "jun" may be a spurious addition.
translations.idiomatic: Either "tai" or "jun" may be a spurious addition.

sentences.zh: 可更為誦悲彭城詩 諸本「更」作「便」，北史卷四七祖瑩傳、冊府卷八五０

translations.literal: Regarding "he could again recite the Lament for Pengcheng": various editions read "geng" (again) as "bian" (then); the biography of Zu Ying in juan 47 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 850
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "he could again recite the Lament for Pengcheng": various editions read "geng" (again) as "bian" (then); the biography of Zu Ying in juan 47 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 850

sentences.zh: 〈一０一一二頁〉
作「更」。

translations.literal: read "geng" (again).
translations.idiomatic: read "geng" (again).

sentences.zh: 按上稱「勰欲使肅更詠」。

translations.literal: Above the text reads "Xie wished to have Su recite again."
translations.idiomatic: Above the text reads "Xie wished to have Su recite again."

sentences.zh: 「便」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "bian" is erroneous; the text is corrected here on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The character "bian" is erroneous; the text is corrected here on that authority.

sentences.zh: 不尋致服之情 北史卷四二常爽附常景傳、冊府卷五八一

translations.literal: Regarding "does not pursue the feelings of mourning garments": the biography of Chang Jing appended to Chang Shuang in juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 581
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "does not pursue the feelings of mourning garments": the biography of Chang Jing appended to Chang Shuang in juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties and Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 581

sentences.zh: 〈六九六二頁〉

translations.literal: read "zhi" (bring about) as "zhi" (prescribe).
translations.idiomatic: read "zhi" (bring about) as "zhi" (prescribe).

sentences.zh: 按所論即在「制服」，疑作「制」是。

translations.literal: The discussion concerns "prescribing mourning garments"; "zhi" (prescribe) is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: The passage concerns "prescribing mourning garments"; "zhi" (prescribe) is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 時肅宗行講學之禮於國子寺 諸本「行」訛「以」，今據北史卷四二常爽附常景傳改。

translations.literal: Regarding "at that time Emperor Suzong conducted the rite of lecturing at the Imperial Academy": various editions wrongly read "xing" (conduct) as "yi" (by); the text is corrected here according to the biography of Chang Jing appended to Chang Shuang in juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "at that time Emperor Suzong conducted the rite of lecturing at the Imperial Academy": various editions wrongly read "xing" (conduct) as "yi" (by); the text is corrected here according to the biography of Chang Jing appended to Chang Shuang in juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 俄而安州石離冗城斛鹽三戍兵反 冊府卷三五四

translations.literal: Regarding "soon afterward the garrisons of Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province rebelled": Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 354
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "soon afterward the garrisons of Shili, Rongcheng, and Huyan in An Province rebelled": Cefu Yuan Gui, juan 354

sentences.zh: 〈四一九九頁〉
「冗城」作「宛城」。

translations.literal: reads "Rongcheng" as "Wancheng."
translations.idiomatic: reads "Rongcheng" as "Wancheng."

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一五一

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151

sentences.zh: 〈四七一０頁〉
作「穴城」，胡注以見於水經注卷一四鮑丘水篇的「孔山」當之。

translations.literal: reads "Xuecheng" (Cave City); Hu Sanxing's note identifies it with "Kong Mountain" mentioned in the Baoqiu River chapter, juan 14, of the Commentary on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: reads "Xuecheng" (Cave City); Hu Sanxing's note identifies it with "Kong Mountain" mentioned in the Baoqiu River chapter, juan 14, of the Commentary on the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 按水經注稱孔山「上有洞穴開明」，其地與斛鹽戍鄰接。

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Water Classic says of Kong Mountain that "above it are caves opening to the light"; that place adjoins the Huyan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Water Classic says of Kong Mountain that "above it are caves opening to the light"; that place adjoins the Huyan garrison.

sentences.zh: 百衲本「冗」字末筆稍直，疑實是「穴」字缺上點，冊府作「宛」雖誤，上也作「宀」可證。

translations.literal: In the Baibaina edition the final stroke of "rong" is slightly straight; it is suspected to be "xue" (cave) with the upper dot missing. Although Cefu reads "wan," which is wrong, its upper component is also "mi" (roof radical), which supports this.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baibaina edition the final stroke of "rong" is slightly straight; it is likely "xue" (cave) with the upper dot missing. Although Cefu reads "wan," which is wrong, its upper component is also "mi" (roof radical), which supports this.

sentences.zh: 自松岍赴賊 通鑑卷一五一

translations.literal: Regarding "he set out from Songqian to meet the rebels": Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "he set out from Songqian to meet the rebels": Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151

sentences.zh: 〈四七一０頁〉
胡注：「或曰：『岍』『𡶭』字之誤也，讀作『陘』。

translations.literal: Hu Sanxing's note: "Some say 'qian' and '𡶭' are erroneous characters and should be read as 'xing' (pass).
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing's note: "Some say 'qian' and '𡶭' are erroneous characters and should be read as 'xing' (pass).

sentences.zh: 唐志

translations.literal: The Tang Geographic Treatise
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Geographic Treatise

sentences.zh: 〈唐書卷四三下地理志下載入四夷道路〉

translations.literal: 〈New Book of Tang, juan 43B, Geographic Treatise, section on Roads into the Four Barbarian Regions〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈New Book of Tang, juan 43B, Geographic Treatise, section on Roads into the Four Barbarian Regions〉

sentences.zh: 營州西北有松陘嶺。」

translations.literal: Northwest of Ying Province is Songxing Ridge."
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Ying Province is Songxing Ridge."

sentences.zh: 率屬城人禦之 通志卷一五０上常景傳「率」上有「景」字。

translations.literal: Regarding "he led the people of the subordinate city to resist them": in the biography of Chang Jing in juan 150, part 1, of the Tongzhi, the character "Jing" appears before "led."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "he led the people of the subordinate city to resist them": the biography of Chang Jing in juan 150, part 1, of the Tongzhi has the character "Jing" before "led."

sentences.zh: 按此字不宜省，當是脫文。

translations.literal: This character should not be omitted; it is probably a lacuna in the text.
translations.idiomatic: This character should not be omitted; it is probably a lacuna in the text.

sentences.zh: 景與都督于榮刺史王延年置兵粟園 諸本「粟園」作「粟國」，卷九肅宗紀孝昌二年七月作「粟園」，通鑑卷一五一

translations.literal: Regarding "Jing, together with Commander-in-Chief Yu Rong and Prefect Wang Yannian, deployed troops at Sugarden": various editions read "Sugarden" as "Suguo"; the annals of Emperor Suzong in juan 9, seventh month of the second year of Xiaochang, read "Sugarden"; Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Jing, together with Commander-in-Chief Yu Rong and Prefect Wang Yannian, deployed troops at Sugarden": various editions read "Sugarden" as "Suguo"; the annals of Emperor Suzong in juan 9, seventh month of the second year of Xiaochang, read "Sugarden"; Zizhi Tongjian, juan 151

sentences.zh: 〈四七一四頁〉
作「栗園」。

translations.literal: reads "Liyuan" (Chestnut Garden).
translations.idiomatic: reads "Liyuan" (Chestnut Garden).

sentences.zh: 按「國」字必訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "guo" (state) is certainly erroneous; the text is corrected here on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: The character "guo" (state) is certainly erroneous; the text is corrected here on that authority.

sentences.zh: 「粟」疑亦當作「栗」，但諸本及紀皆同，今仍之。

translations.literal: "Su" (millet) is also suspected to read "li" (chestnut), but all editions and the annals agree; the text is left unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: "Su" (millet) may also read "li" (chestnut), but all editions and the annals agree; the text is left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 參卷九校記粟園條。

translations.literal: See the collation note on Sugarden in juan 9.
translations.idiomatic: See the collation note on Sugarden in juan 9.

sentences.zh: 原夫人□之度 諸本「人」下不空格，北史卷四二注「闕」字。

translations.literal: Regarding "the original lady □'s measure": various editions leave no blank space after "ren" (person); juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties marks a character as "deficient."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "the original lady □'s measure": various editions leave no blank space after "ren" (person); juan 42 of the History of the Northern Dynasties marks a character as deficient.

sentences.zh: 按若如諸本，與下「勢位之危」句不相對，「人」下當闕一字，今作方圍。

translations.literal: If the various editions are followed, the line does not parallel the following phrase "the peril of rank and position"; one character after "ren" must be missing, and a square is used here to mark the lacuna.
translations.idiomatic: If the various editions are followed, the line does not parallel the following phrase "the peril of rank and position"; one character after "ren" must be missing, and a square is used here to mark the lacuna.
